{"notes": "Visit 5 (5:45). Table: top line intact. Bottom line is dark from the start to x~18. A pale jammed cluster sits at x18-19.5, y12-14. Dark dominoes continue past it and the tail curl is dark, so the fall mostly reaches the tail. The tail is still a rounded curl with no pointed fin. The dark stray loop (x19-22, y12-13) is still there, and it may be what links the tail to the body, so clearing it carelessly could break the chain. The pale off-pad curve to y~18 is gone, so someone cleared it. Leo's hands were at x24.5, y13.5, at the end of the lower spur.

LEO: Says top and bottom lines and the fin are standing. He admits the fin came out rounder than planned, which is honest. He says he's closing the break 'just before the tail', but his hands are about 6 units from the pale jam at x18-19. Claims still run ahead of output. No pointed fin. He did stay in scope and left the loop and tail join to Priya.

MAYA: Accurate, calm status. Stays off the fin, apologised for an earlier false alarm, and her inspection matches what I see. Reliable, with good collaboration and self-awareness. Her bottom line is done.

TOM: Says he joined the bottom and removed off-pad strays. The off-pad curve is gone, which fits his claim, but I can't confirm it was him. Maya credits him and Priya for the join. His nose check is still unverified. Ask him exactly what he did.

PRIYA: Gives the clearest status (about 96 of 111). Delegates well and owns the loop clearing, the tail join and the jam cleanup. Loop and jam are still unresolved. Ask whether the loop is load-bearing.

Next: is the loop cleared without breaking the chain? Is the jam fixed? Who did the join?"}
